children.text: For the past six years, the Vermont Health Information Exchange (VHIE) has operated on a modular 'best-of-breed' architecture, integrating disparate components for MPI, FHIR repositories, and terminology services. While this served the initial phase of data liquidity, the market has matured. Technology is now a commodity, and the state's imperative must shift from infrastructure maintenance to solving the nation's highest cost of care per capita.

Maintaining individual contracts and integration points for vendors like Verato and Medicasoft creates significant overhead. This 'plumbing' distraction forces leadership to focus on API management and server uptime rather than clinical outcomes. Every upgrade risks breaking the ecosystem, requiring continuous, expensive engineering hours.
In the current mature market, building your own HIE infrastructure is akin to a hospital building its own MRI machines rather than buying them from Siemens or GE.

The recommended path is to adopt the CSS 'HIE in a Box' model, a non-profit support organization serving 9+ states. This shifts VHIE from a 'Builder' model to a 'Subscriber' model, leveraging massive economies of scale.

body.title: Comparison: Modular Architecture vs. CSS Utility Model

children.text: Shifting to CSS converts volatile CapEx (major upgrades) into predictable OpEx, freeing capital for community health programs. Furthermore, this aligns with CMS and ONC strategies to treat HIEs as health data utilities under TEFCA. The CSS platform already includes advanced modules for claims integration and image exchange, allowing Vermont to deploy capabilities immediately rather than building them from scratch.

body.summary: A strategic overview of why HIEs must transition from technology builders to data utility subscribers.
body.title: Executive Brief: The End of the Builder Era

summary: Vermont faces a critical strategic choice: continue funding a fragmented, high-maintenance modular HIE architecture or pivot to a shared utility model. This analysis advocates for the immediate adoption of CRISP Shared Services (CSS), leveraging multi-state economies of scale to address Vermont's unsustainable healthcare cost trajectory.
title: Strategic Pivot: Transitioning VHIE to the CRISP Shared Services Utility Model
